marble.name: Money word problems
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately
marble.prompt: If you has 2 quarters, 1 dime, and 3 pennies, can they work out the total — and tell you whether that's enough to buy something costing 65 cents?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning about measurement in everyday life — telling time to the hour and half-hour, comparing lengths and weights of objects, understanding money, and using time words like yesterday and tomorrow.

misconceptions: Value = size: a bigger coin is worth more (nickel > dime; five pennies > three dimes)
Value = count: each coin counts as one, or all coins are counted by ones regardless of denomination (unitary thinking)
Cannot switch counting patterns — counts 25, 50, 75 then cannot shift to +10 for a dime or +1 for a penny
Notation errors — mixing $ and ¢ ($0.50¢, or $5 for a nickel), or writing 5¢ as $5
Overusing one denomination (all dimes) because counting by tens is easiest, rather than realistic combinations
representations: Proportional value strips / 'proportional dollar' (a coin laid over its worth in unit-squares)
A number line or hundred-square for skip-counting coin values
A coin-value reference (penny 1¢, nickel 5¢, dime 10¢, quarter 25¢, dollar 100¢)
A part-whole bar for making change (cost and amount paid)
authoredAnswer: Totals 2 dimes + 3 pennies as 23¢ by counting 10, 20, then 21, 22, 23; states three dimes (30¢) is worth more than five pennies (5¢) and justifies by value, not size or number of coins; assembles 46¢ and gives 6¢ change; writes amounts using ¢ (or $ with a decimal) correctly without mixing the two.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Chooses the bigger or more-numerous set as 'worth more'; on a total, treats the nickel as greater than the dime
wrongAnswers.fix: Lay each coin over its proportional value (dime = 10 unit-squares) so worth is seen apart from size; confront this preoperational value-equals-size heuristic directly

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Says 2 dimes + 3 pennies is '5', or counts 1,2,3,4,5 touching each coin rather than counting on by value
wrongAnswers.fix: Reteach that a coin's value is a number of cents you count on, using proportional manipulatives; start from one denomination before mixing

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Counts 25, 50, 75 then adds a dime as '76' or restarts the count; overrelies on dimes to avoid switching
wrongAnswers.fix: Practise counting on from the largest coin, scaffolding the switch with a number line; reteach place-value-based counting

before.name: Fluent adding and subtracting within 100
before.reason: Money word problems require fluent addition/subtraction within 100
